The Profile Likelihood of Coefficients

Source: R/profile.R
statmod_profile.Rd

Returns, for each combination of values of one or several coefficients, the maximum of the penalized log-likelihood over all the other coefficients when those are held at the values. The result is a data frame, one row per combination, which serves a plot, an interval or a diagnostic; the function computes none of those.

Usage

statmod_profile(
  fit,
  which,
  values = profile_range(width = 3, n = 21),
  method = profile_grid(),
  hyper = c("held", "refit"),
  cores = 1
)

Arguments

fit

A StatmodFit().

which

A character vector of unique labels "parameter:coefficient", of one equation or of several.

values

Either one profile_range(), which applies to every coefficient of which, or a list. The named elements of a list carry names of which and are numeric vectors (the values, on the scale described above) or profile_range() objects. At most one element without a name sets the default for the coefficients that no element names, and without it that default is profile_range(). Two unnamed elements, or a name that is not in which, are errors. The values of each coefficient are sorted increasingly and repeated values are dropped. With several coefficients the table has one row for each combination of values, and the first coefficient varies fastest.

method

A profile_method: profile_grid().

hyper

"held" or "refit": whether the hyperparameters stay at the values of the fit or are searched again at every point.

cores

The number of separate R processes over which the refits are distributed, a single whole number (default 1, no process besides this one). It is distinct from the threads of statmod(), which counts threads inside one process; a refit that runs in a separate process is sequential. Under pkgload the run stays sequential.

Value

A data frame (check.names = FALSE) with one column for each coefficient of which, named by its label, then profile_loglik, profile_penalty, profile_pen_loglik, outer_criterion and converged. Its attributes are maximum, a one-row data frame with the same columns at the unrestricted fit (the numbers of the fit itself, which under reml() or ml() can lie slightly below the nearest rows of the table, because at a row the criterion does not integrate the held coefficients), method, the profile_method object, hyper, and criterion, the outer criterion object of the fit (NULL if it has none). The hyperparameters and the other coefficients of each point are not returned.

What the columns report

The columns profile_loglik, profile_penalty and profile_pen_loglik belong to the INNER criterion, the penalized log-likelihood of the coefficients at the hyperparameters in force. At the point where the coefficients are held at the values of the row, profile_loglik is the log-likelihood without the penalty, profile_penalty is the penalty with the sign that makes the two add up, that is the logarithm of the prior density of the coefficients, \(-\tfrac12 P_\lambda(\beta)\) with its normalizing constant, and profile_pen_loglik is their sum, which is the quantity that the refit maximizes. The constant depends on the hyperparameters and not on the coefficients, so the penalty is not necessarily negative, and with the hyperparameters held its changes along the grid are those of the quadratic form. A model without penalty has profile_penalty equal to zero, and the two log-likelihoods then coincide.

The column outer_criterion belongs to the OUTER criterion (reml(), ml(), aic() or bic()), a different function of a different object: the value, on the sign and the scale that the fit reports in fit@criterion, of the criterion that chooses the hyperparameters or the coefficients that the criterion estimates. It is not the profile of that criterion over the held coefficients in any sense that the first three columns have for the inner one, and it is NA when the point involved no outer search: when the fit has no outer criterion, or when the hyperparameters are held (hyper = "held") and the criterion estimates no coefficient.

The column converged states that the point is at the maximum of its refit. It is TRUE when the stopping rule of the refit fired, or when the Newton decrement at the point is below the tolerance of statmod_certificate(), and in both cases the final inner fit converged. The second condition is needed because the line search of the outer optimizer can exhaust its backtracks at a point that is already the optimum, without recording that its stopping rule fired. The row of the attribute maximum reports instead fit@converged, which is only the flag of the stopping rule. A refit that signals an error gives a row of NA with converged = FALSE, and the function warns.

The coefficients to hold: which

A label has the form "parameter:coefficient": the distribution parameter whose equation carries the coefficient, a colon, and the name of the coefficient as the second column of the table of coef_labels() gives it, which is the name that coef() and summary() print. The labels of a fit are the row names of summary(fit), for example "mu:(Intercept)", "mu:x" or "sigma:s(z).1". Labels must be unique.

The coefficient of the effect of a covariate z on the parameter theta of a modelterms7::nl() term, written nl(~ a * exp(-theta * x), theta ~ 1 + z) in the equation of mu, has the label "mu:nl.theta.z". The name after the colon is nl., the name of the parameter of the term, a dot and the name of the coefficient of its subformula, so that the intercept of theta is "mu:nl.theta.(Intercept)". A parameter of the term without a subformula is a coefficient by itself, as in "mu:nl.a".

The position of a break-point of modelterms7::seg() is the coefficient psi1 (then psi2, and so on) of the term, as in "mu:seg.psi1". When the position has a subformula, as in seg(w, psi ~ x), its coefficients are "mu:seg.psi1.(Intercept)" and "mu:seg.psi1.x". The names of all the coefficients of a fit are the row names of statmodels7:::coef_labels(fit@spec, statmodels7:::statmod_design(fit@spec)).

When two or more positions of the same seg() term without subformulas are in which, the positions of a model are ordered and distinct: the combinations of the grid in which a position is not larger than the position before it are not evaluated and are not in the table.

The scale

The values are on the scale of the coefficient in the stacked vector of the fit, which is unconstrained: a coefficient of a linear predictor is on the scale of the link, and so are the coefficients of the predictor of a parameter of a nonlinear term, the positions of the break-points and the parameters of a covariance structure. Values on another scale must be mapped to it by the caller. A monotone map relabels the grid and leaves the columns of the profile unchanged.

The hyperparameters, and the coefficients of the criterion

With hyper = "held" the hyperparameters (the smoothing parameters and the scales of the random effects) stay at the values of the fit, and with hyper = "refit" the outer search is run again at every point. In both cases, when the outer criterion estimates coefficients (reml() and ml() estimate the unpenalized coefficients of every parameter except the first), those coefficients are estimated by the criterion at every point and are not carried to the joint mode of the penalized likelihood, which statmod_restrict() does. A held coefficient that the criterion would have estimated is held, and the criterion estimates the rest. The cost of a point is then that of an outer search over those coordinates, and it exceeds the cost of a restricted fit.

The outer optimizer is the default one of statmod(), and the stopping rules, the inner method and the information are those of the fit.

Coefficients that cannot be held yet

A coefficient under a penalty with a kink (a lasso, a SCAD or an MCP), a coefficient of a model with a structural term (modelterms7::gas(), modelterms7::regime(), the marginal break-point term) and any coefficient with hyper = "refit" in a model whose kinked penalties are tuned by a path signal an error. An aliased coefficient has no estimate to profile and signals an error.

See also

profile_grid(), profile_range(), statmod_test() for the likelihood ratio at one value.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(60))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(60, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)

# the profile of the slope, on five standard errors
prof <- statmod_profile(fit, which = "mu:x",
                        values = profile_range(width = 2, n = 9))
prof
#>       mu:x profile_loglik profile_penalty profile_pen_loglik outer_criterion
#> 1 1.615742      -23.56354               0          -23.56354       -25.70965
#> 2 1.700842      -22.70458               0          -22.70458       -24.86501
#> 3 1.785942      -22.07563               0          -22.07563       -24.24654
#> 4 1.871043      -21.69183               0          -21.69183       -23.86914
#> 5 1.956143      -21.56280               0          -21.56280       -23.74225
#> 6 2.041243      -21.69183               0          -21.69183       -23.86914
#> 7 2.126343      -22.07563               0          -22.07563       -24.24654
#> 8 2.211443      -22.70458               0          -22.70458       -24.86501
#> 9 2.296543      -23.56354               0          -23.56354       -25.70965
#>   converged
#> 1      TRUE
#> 2      TRUE
#> 3      TRUE
#> 4      TRUE
#> 5      TRUE
#> 6      TRUE
#> 7      TRUE
#> 8      TRUE
#> 9      TRUE

# the log-likelihood falls by z^2 / 2 at z standard errors
attr(prof, "maximum")
#>       mu:x profile_loglik profile_penalty profile_pen_loglik outer_criterion
#> 1 1.956143      -21.57563               0          -21.57563       -24.59838
#>   converged
#> 1      TRUE

# two coefficients, with values chosen by the caller for the second
statmod_profile(fit, which = c("mu:x", "mu:(Intercept)"),
                values = list("mu:x" = profile_range(width = 1, n = 3),
                              "mu:(Intercept)" = c(0.8, 1, 1.2)))
#>       mu:x mu:(Intercept) profile_loglik profile_penalty profile_pen_loglik
#> 1 1.785942            0.8      -43.60960               0          -43.60960
#> 2 1.956143            0.8      -35.87738               0          -35.87738
#> 3 2.126343            0.8      -29.40230               0          -29.40230
#> 4 1.785942            1.0      -27.66303               0          -27.66303
#> 5 1.956143            1.0      -22.79422               0          -22.79422
#> 6 2.126343            1.0      -22.13489               0          -22.13489
#> 7 1.785942            1.2      -22.49681               0          -22.49681
#> 8 1.956143            1.2      -25.44694               0          -25.44694
#> 9 2.126343            1.2      -31.78035               0          -31.78035
#>   outer_criterion converged
#> 1       -43.60960      TRUE
#> 2       -35.87738      TRUE
#> 3       -29.40230      TRUE
#> 4       -27.66303      TRUE
#> 5       -22.79422      TRUE
#> 6       -22.13489      TRUE
#> 7       -22.49681      TRUE
